messages.subject: Multistate model JAGS - Including age structure in variables constrained to sum 1 (Dirichlet prior)
parts:
Hello all,

I am building a multistate model with survival and two different types of recruitment for a long-lived animal species using JAGS. My data includes live encounters and dead recoveries. From one occasion to another, my model includes three different possibilities in terms of recruitment: "recruitment of type A", "recruitment of type B" and "not recruited".This implies having to constraint recruitment probabilities to sum to 1 altogether using a Dirichlet prior following Kéry and Schaub (2012), which successfully worked in my models. However, my next step is to add an age structure with 5 age classes to all types of recruitment, and I am struggling to find a correct way to model this: I've tried several coding alternatives and I keep getting error notes.

Here's the code for modelling recruitments as constant probabilities:

#States:
#1: Alive, not recruited
#2: Alive, recruited A
#3: Alive, recruited B
#4: Dead, not recruited
#5: Dead, recruited
#6: Long-dead
cat("
    model{
    #Priors and constraints
    for(i in 1:nind){
    for(t in f[i]:(n.occasions-1)){ 
    phi[i,t] <- surv[ages[i,t]]
    p[i,t] <- recap[ages[i,t]]
    r[i,t] <- mean.r
    }#t
    }#i
    for(u in 1:5){
    surv[u] ~ dunif(0,1)
    recap[u] ~ dunif(0,1)
    }
    mean.r ~ dunif(0,1)
    #Gamma priors for recruitment and emigration (Dirichlet)
    for (i in 1:3){ #1: not recruiting, 2: recruitment A, 3: recruitment B
    a[i] ~ dgamma(1,1) #Hyperprior for recruitment
    psiR[i] <- a[i]/sum(a[])
    }
    #Define state-transition and observation matrices
    for(i in 1:nind){
    for(t in f[i]:(n.occasions-1)){
    #State transition matrix
    ps[1,i,t,1] <- phi[i,t]*psiR[1] #Not recruiting
    ps[1,i,t,2] <- phi[i,t]*psiR[2] #Recruitment A
    ps[1,i,t,3] <- phi[i,t]*psiR[3] #Recruitment B
    ps[1,i,t,4] <- (1-phi[i,t])*(psiR[1])*r[i,t]
    ps[1,i,t,5] <- ((1-phi[i,t])*psiR[2]*r[i,t]) + ((1-phi[i,t])*psiR[3]*r[i,t])
    ps[1,i,t,6] <- 0
    ps[2,i,t,1] <- 0
    ps[2,i,t,2] <- phi[i,t]
    ps[2,i,t,3] <- 0
    ps[2,i,t,4] <- 0
    ps[2,i,t,5] <- (1-phi[i,t])*r[i,t]
    ps[2,i,t,6] <- 0
    ps[3,i,t,1] <- 0
    ps[3,i,t,2] <- 0
    ps[3,i,t,3] <- phi[i,t]
    ps[3,i,t,4] <- 0
    ps[3,i,t,5] <- (1-phi[i,t])*r[i,t]
    ps[3,i,t,6] <- 0
    ps[4,i,t,1] <- 0
    ps[4,i,t,2] <- 0
    ps[4,i,t,3] <- 0
    ps[4,i,t,4] <- 0
    ps[4,i,t,5] <- 0
    ps[4,i,t,6] <- 1
    ps[5,i,t,1] <- 0
    ps[5,i,t,2] <- 0
    ps[5,i,t,3] <- 0
    ps[5,i,t,4] <- 0
    ps[5,i,t,5] <- 0
    ps[5,i,t,6] <- 1
    ps[6,i,t,1] <- 0
    ps[6,i,t,2] <- 0
    ps[6,i,t,3] <- 0
    ps[6,i,t,4] <- 0
    ps[6,i,t,5] <- 0
    ps[6,i,t,6] <- 1
    #Observation probabilities
    po[1,i,t,1] <- p[i,t]
    po[1,i,t,2] <- 0
    po[1,i,t,3] <- 0
    po[1,i,t,4] <- 0
    po[1,i,t,5] <- 0
    po[1,i,t,6] <- 1-p[i,t]
    po[2,i,t,1] <- 0
    po[2,i,t,2] <- p[i,t]
    po[2,i,t,3] <- 0
    po[2,i,t,4] <- 0
    po[2,i,t,5] <- 0
    po[2,i,t,6] <- 1-p[i,t]
    po[3,i,t,1] <- 0
    po[3,i,t,2] <- 0
    po[3,i,t,3] <- p[i,t]
    po[3,i,t,4] <- 0
    po[3,i,t,5] <- 0
    po[3,i,t,6] <- 1-p[i,t]
    po[4,i,t,1] <- 0
    po[4,i,t,2] <- 0
    po[4,i,t,3] <- 0
    po[4,i,t,4] <- 1
    po[4,i,t,5] <- 0
    po[4,i,t,6] <- 0
    po[5,i,t,1] <- 0
    po[5,i,t,2] <- 0
    po[5,i,t,3] <- 0
    po[5,i,t,4] <- 0
    po[5,i,t,5] <- 1
    po[5,i,t,6] <- 0
    po[6,i,t,1] <- 0
    po[6,i,t,2] <- 0
    po[6,i,t,3] <- 0
    po[6,i,t,4] <- 0
    po[6,i,t,5] <- 0
    po[6,i,t,6] <- 1
      }#t
    }#i
    # Likelihood
    for (i in 1:nind){
    # Define latent state at first capture
    z[i,f[i]] <- y[i,f[i]]
    for (t in (f[i]+1):n.occasions){
    # State process: draw S(t) given S(t-1)
    z[i,t] ~ dcat(ps[z[i,t-1], i, t-1,])
    # Observation process: draw O(t) given S(t)
    y[i,t] ~ dcat(po[z[i,t], i, t-1,])
} #t
} #i
}
    ",fill=TRUE)

Note the age structure is already incorporated in other parameters and works successfully.

Any ideas or suggestions would be very appreciated. Please let me know if you need any further details.

Happy new year all! Thanks,

Jaume

In case anybody is interested or finds themselves in the same trouble, I finally found the way to model my case correctly. Basically, a simple yet optimal way appears to be to parameterize the age effect in the transitions.

cat("
    model{
    #Priors and constraints
    for(i in 1:nind){
    for(t in f[i]:(n.occasions-1)){ 
    phi[i,t] <- surv[ages[i,t]]
    p[i,t] <- recap[ages[i,t]]
    r[i,t] <- mean.r
    }#t

    for(u in 1:5){
    surv[u] ~ dunif(0,1)
    recap[u] ~ dunif(0,1)
    }
    mean.r ~ dunif(0,1)

#Gamma priors for recruitment (Dirichlet)
     for (r in 1:3){
     for (age in 1:5){
     a[r,age] ~ dgamma(1,1) #Hyperprior
     psiR[r,age] <- a[r,age]/sum(a[,age])

}
     }
    #Define state-transition and observation matrices
    for(i in 1:nind){
    for(t in f[i]:(n.occasions-1)){
    #State transition matrix

ps[1,i,t,1] <- phi[i,t]*psiR[1,ages[i,t]] #Not Recruiting
    ps[1,i,t,2] <- phi[i,t]*psiR[2,ages[i,t]] #Recruitment A

ps[1,i,t,6] <- 0

    ps[5,i,t,5] <- 0
